document.description: PA5388 encodes CaiX, the periplasmic carnitine-recognition subunit associated with the shared CbcWV ABC importer in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1. Its signal peptide directs export, while the substrate-binding domain supplies carnitine recognition to the membrane permease and ATPase. P. aeruginosa genetics and reconstitution of compatible CbcWV/CaiX proteins establish import rather than a chemical step of carnitine degradation. Substrate uptake kinetics are properties of the assembled transport system, not purified CaiX binding constants.

review.summary: The uptake assays show carnitine transport, but carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound, and GO does not place carnitine transport under amine transport.
review.reason: The experiment supports the carnitine-specific term already on this protein (GO:0015226). An OLS4 query of the GO hierarchy (PSEPK/cbcW/cbcW-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md, hierarchicalAncestors, run 2026-11-04) shows GO:0015226, GO:0015879 and GO:1902603 sit under quaternary ammonium group transport (GO:0015697/GO:0015651) and not under GO:0005275 or GO:0015837. The amine term is therefore a lateral mis-placement of the substrate class, not a true-but-broad ancestor, and is replaced rather than kept as non-core. The genes/human/SLC22A5 review keeps GO:0015837 on a carnitine transporter as correct but general; the difference from that precedent is deliberate and follows the OLS placement.

document.description: CbcV (PA5376) is the ATP-binding and hydrolyzing component of the Cbc ABC importer in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1. It energizes the CbcW membrane component, while associated binding proteins specify choline, glycine betaine, carnitine and, in characterized CosX-containing combinations, choline-O-sulfate. Its ATPase acts on the cytoplasmic side of the transport assembly by the conserved ABC mechanism. Substrate import supplies nutrients for downstream catabolic enzymes; CbcV is not a sulfate-specific pump or a substrate-degrading enzyme.

document.description: CbcW (PA5377) is the multipass inner-membrane permease of the shared Cbc ABC importer in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1. document.description: BcoE-BcoF is a fused dehydrogenase–thioesterase of Sinorhizobium meliloti carnitine metabolism. Its N-terminal region oxidizes L-carnitine to 3-dehydrocarnitine with NAD+, and its C-terminal hotdog region hydrolyzes betainyl-CoA to glycine betaine and CoA. The same protein also hydrolyzes carnitinyl-CoA, releasing carnitine during upstream gamma-butyrobetaine utilization. These three activities were measured on the sequence-matched 3D0a2 protein. Native GBB-growth phenotypes differ between Rm2011 and strain 1021 despite identical local coding sequences.

document.summary: NAD-dependent dehydrogenases with the 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase N-terminal NAD-binding (3HCDH_N) and C-terminal (3HCDH) domains. The reviewed members fall into several functional groups. SF5 mixes bacterial 3-hydroxybutyryl-CoA dehydrogenases (Clostridium Hbd, Bacillus MmgB), the 3-hydroxyadipyl-CoA dehydrogenase PaaH of phenylacetate catabolism, and L-carnitine dehydrogenases (EC 1.1.1.108), some of which (Rhizobiales and Roseobacter CdhAB/BcoE-BcoF) carry a C-terminal betainyl-CoA thioesterase region. SF9 holds mycobacterial FadB2. SF1 includes characterized animal lambda-crystallins (L-gulonate 3-dehydrogenase) and nonanimal homologs, and SF7 includes the Bacillus FadN hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase with an additional hydratase-like domain; other members require separate substrate and architecture assessment.
document.coherence_reason: Every characterized member is an NAD-dependent oxidoreductase acting on a CH-OH group, but the substrate differs between and within subfamilies: acyl-CoA thioesters (Hbd, PaaH, FadB2), the free quaternary-amine acid L-carnitine (CdhA/LcdH), and L-gulonate (lambda-crystallin). SF5 itself contains both 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenases and L-carnitine dehydrogenases, so neither the carnitine nor the acyl-CoA substrate transfers from the subfamily label.

module.title: Bacterial L-carnitine catabolism through 3-dehydrocarnitine
module.description: An aerobic bacterial pathway that converts L-carnitine to glycine betaine through 3-dehydrocarnitine. An NAD-dependent L-carnitine dehydrogenase forms 3-dehydrocarnitine; a beta-keto acid cleavage enzyme (CdhC/BcoG) transfers the trimethylammonio-acetyl (betainyl) group to acetyl-CoA, releasing acetoacetate and forming betainyl-CoA; and a betainyl-CoA thioesterase releases glycine betaine and free CoA. The thioesterase is either a separate hotdog-fold protein (CdhB) or the C-terminal region of a bifunctional dehydrogenase-thioesterase (CdhAB/BcoE-BcoF). Where carnitine is taken up through an ABC importer, the CaiX substrate-binding protein confers carnitine selectivity on the shared CbcWV choline/betaine/carnitine core. The oxygenolytic CntAB route to trimethylamine, anaerobic Cai reduction to gamma-butyrobetaine, compatible-solute retention, acetoacetate activation, and downstream glycine-betaine demethylation are outside this boundary.

module.notes:
The context is Pseudomonadota, with supported gamma- and alphaproteobacterial realizers, not a claim of universal pathway occurrence. The defined reaction boundary starts at free L-carnitine and ends at glycine betaine. Upstream gamma-butyrobetaine conversion, downstream GB demethylation, compatible-solute retention, CntAB trimethylamine production and Cai-dependent anaerobic reduction are separate mechanisms. The reactions themselves do not consume molecular oxygen; aerobic denotes the characterized physiological setting, not an oxygen substrate requirement. Anaerobic CJ25 GB production in PMID:40853000 proposes different downstream chemistry and does not establish this exact betainyl-CoA route.

CaiX-CbcWV import is optional because free carnitine may be supplied by other importers or upstream intracellular synthesis. PAO1 CbcWV proteins have direct construct provenance, with native PA14/PAO1 and heterologous-host assay boundaries recorded in their reviews. KT2440 transport and LcdH/CdhB chemistry rely on target architecture, conserved locus and characterized orthologs; the purified P. putida enzyme in PMID:3058208 is from IFP206. KT2440 PP_0303 is an exception to the former blanket unassayed claim: PMID:24240508 Data Sets 2/4 map Q88R31 to BKACE511 and record direct substrate screening. Its raw KAH signal lacks a recovered positive-call threshold, so possible secondary KAH activity remains unresolved; this neither establishes lysine metabolism nor negates its carnitine role. PANTHER BKACE or hydroxyacyl-CoA family membership alone is insufficient to select the exact reaction.

For the fused Sinorhizobium realization, cloned 3D0a2 proteins were identical to Rm2011 and independently match the strain 1021 representative sequences. Full-length BcoEF supplies both oxidation and betainyl-CoA hydrolysis; isolated-domain assays and substrate channeling were not demonstrated. Its additional carnitinyl-CoA hydrolysis belongs upstream of this module. Rm1021 GBB-growth failure despite locus identity is retained as a strain-specific phenotype, not a negative carnitine-enzyme assay. The paper's mutant set excludes BcoG; its role is supported by catalytic measurements, not an invented knockout.

Broad GO parents GO:0016747 and GO:0016289 do not by themselves identify CdhC or CdhB specificity. The exact substrates/products, EC/Rhea reaction evidence, reviewed representatives and member-level activity constraints define each step. Both families are heterogeneous, and the fused thioesterase is grounded as an ortholog realization rather than assigning its domain an unverified PANTHER id. No complete pathway is inferred from a single dehydrogenase or from carnitine/GB growth alone.
